subtype: Approach: putting things back in the same place each day [Thinking]
passage: The bell for maths rang and thirty bags unzipped at once. Pema, at the next desk, was already pulling out books, a pencil case, a sticky water bottle, half a packet of biscuits. Lokesh did not look down. His hand slid into the front pocket and came back with the geometry box. "How do you always find it so fast?" Pema whispered. "It lives there," Lokesh whispered back. "Front pocket, box. Back pocket, diary. I decided in Class 5 and never changed it." He thought: if it goes back in the same spot, my hand will know without my head. Pema found her compass under the biscuits and groaned.

qa.q: Where does Lokesh keep his diary?
qa.a: His diary lives in the back pocket.

qa.q: What does Lokesh think about putting things back in the same spot?
qa.a: He thinks his hand will know where things are without his head having to remember, which shows he trusts the habit.

qa.q: What other approach could Pema try, and why?
qa.a: Pema could empty her bag and pack it again with a fixed place for each item, since a steady spot saves searching. Checking the bag against a short list at the door could also help.

qa.q: How does the routine look to Pema, who is digging under the biscuits?
qa.a: Pema sees how easy it is for Lokesh and feels a little annoyed at her own mess; the whisper and groan suggest she wants to learn his trick.

grounding: A boy assigns fixed pockets for his geometry box and diary so he need not search when the bell rings.
